_about: Wire contract consumed by Milo-iOS (github.com/leodurandfr/Milo-iOS), a THIRD API client beyond frontend/ and Milo-Mac. Its consumers are short-lived processes — a WidgetKit timeline entry, App Intents — so there is NO WebSocket surface at all: everything is REST, and the app can never be told about a change, only ask. If a route listed here is dropped, Milo-iOS breaks silently at runtime. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for that contract. test_milo_ios_contract.py enforces it offline on every pytest run: the backend still serves every route in `rest`, the manifest matches the VENDORED snapshot's surface exactly, and every payload_invariant holds against the typed response models. check_milo_ios_freshness.py is run BY HAND against a checkout (there is no CI job; 56a3263f dropped it) and refuses to compare at all when a route literal lives outside the vendored file patterns. Refresh the snapshot and this file TOGETHER, consciously, in one commit.
_surface_is_declared_not_reached: The extractor reads the routes MiloAPIClient declares, which is the right granularity for a contract — the app ships that code, and a backend free to delete a route it targets is the hazard. Two of the six are currently declared but invoked by nothing in the app: `getAudioState` and `getDockApps` have no caller in any of the 17 Swift files. They are pinned anyway, because 'no caller today' is a fact about this build and not about the dependency.
_why_this_exists: cf430ae6 deleted GET /api/settings/dock-apps as 'Milo-Mac-only' once the Mac had converged on /bulk. Milo-iOS' client layer targets it too, and nothing in this checkout recorded that. The break is latent rather than live — no caller reaches getDockApps in the published build — so nobody is broken today; the point is that nobody could have known either way. A route with no caller in frontend/src/ is not dead, it is unwitnessed.

_snapshot.note: The MiloAPIClient* files name the routes; Models.swift names the response fields the app decodes. Every call still goes through MiloAPIClient — the Intents and the widget's timeline provider build no URL of their own — but it is no longer ONE file: 09b9789b put the push routes in MiloAPIClient+Push.swift, and Now Playing will add more extensions.
_snapshot.refreshed_without_a_surface_change: Three times now, 09b9789b -> 5e70b79 -> c4cea32b -> efef56dc, no route moved: MiloAPIClient.swift and Models.swift are byte-identical and only MiloAPIClient+Push.swift changed. Refreshed anyway because the vendored copy still held the version that sent the raw `development` entitlement value and took a 422 — a reader consulting it to learn what the app sends would have read code that was wrong, on the very file where that trap occurred. This is NOT a rule to refresh per commit: the test is whether the vendored content would mislead a reader, or whether the surface moved. `check_milo_ios_freshness.py` cannot decide it either way — it compares extracted surfaces, never contents.
_snapshot.why_patterns_not_a_list: The previous snapshot listed exactly two filenames. When the app gained POST /api/push/tokens and DELETE /api/push/tokens/{} in a third file, the extractor read an unchanged surface and the freshness script printed 'vendored snapshot matches upstream' — the contract passing by describing an app that no longer existed, which is the one rot mode _broken_calls.why names. A glob is still a bet on a naming convention, so check_milo_ios_freshness.py::unvendored_surface reads EVERY .swift in a checkout and refuses to compare when a route literal sits outside these patterns. Reported by the app's author, who measured the false green, 2026-09-19.

_broken_calls.why: Routes the app's client layer targets that the backend does not serve. They cannot go in `rest` — test_rest_route_exists would fail on a route that genuinely does not exist — and they cannot be dropped, or the contract would be silent about a dependency that is already unmet. So they are listed, and test_broken_calls_are_still_broken fails the moment either side moves: if the backend starts serving it, or the app stops declaring it, the entry is stale and must go. It is an enumerated fact about the client, never a tolerance in the contract — do not add a second section of this kind to paper over a mismatch.

routes.replacement: Read dock_apps.enabled_apps from GET /api/settings/bulk, already in `rest`. The path survives for PUT, which is why it answers 405 and not 404.

rest.note: Body {delta_db, show_bar}. Built by hand with URLRequest rather than the get/post helper — the extractor reads both shapes on purpose.
Also the only surviving read for dock apps: it carries dock_apps.enabled_apps.

Declared, not reached. Its Codable model (Models.swift::AudioStateResponse) declares a non-optional `status` plus `source`/`title`/`artist`, none of which this route serves — title and artist live inside `metadata`. So the decode would throw if anything called it, and no payload_invariants are listed: asserting fields the app does not read would be inventing a contract rather than recording one.
Answers 200 with status:'error' on failure, not an HTTP error — the same deliberate exception Milo-Mac depends on.

Registers one APNs token (widget / push_to_start / session). Called on every launch; idempotent, so a repeat is free. The app decodes ONE BODY FIELD, `status`, against 'success' — hence the single payload_invariant. Since c4cea32b it ALSO reads the HTTP status and answers registered / refused(detail) / unavailable, keeping a 4xx body verbatim: a 4xx is a verdict on the request, not a transient failure, so it is recorded and never replayed, while a network failure is retried. A refusal is remembered against the token it was about, so a fresh token lifts it. Two call sites reach that retry (didFinishLaunching and didRegisterForRemoteNotifications) and the guard around it is in-flight-aware since efef56dc — read-then-network-then-write left a window where both passed, and an actor did not close it because `await` in an actor method releases isolation. Measured against a stub that refuses: two POSTs became one. Milō could not see it over HTTP — both registrations are idempotent and both answer 200 — but the registry logs every register at INFO, so the duplicate WAS in the journal. The status code is deliberately NOT a payload_invariant: those are resolved by walking this route's OpenAPI RESPONSE SCHEMA, where a status code has no node at all. NOTE on `environment`: this API names the APNs HOSTS (sandbox | production), while Apple's aps-environment entitlement spells the same two values development | production. Milo-iOS forwarded the entitlement verbatim and took a 422 (fixed client-side in 5e70b79, which is where that translation belongs). At the time this client decoded only `status`, so the 422 was indistinguishable from a network failure and the registration silently never happened — that second half is what c4cea32b fixed, and it is why this note now describes a client that can see a refusal. The backend does not accept both spellings: one concept, one key.

Decodes NOTHING from the body — it reads the HTTP status alone and treats 200 AND 404 alike, since a token the backend does not hold is already in the wanted state. No payload_invariants on purpose: asserting a field the app never reads would invent a contract instead of recording one. Hand-built URL with httpMethod = DELETE, the second call shape.

payload_invariants._about: The response fields Milo-iOS decodes by name. A route can survive while the field the app reads is renamed, and a Codable struct missing a non-optional key throws rather than degrading — the whole call fails, it does not lose one value. Resolved through the live OpenAPI schema, never a hand-written copy: `a.b` is a property, `a[k]` a dict value (additionalProperties).
